qt: to the Commission Martin Sonneborn (NI) Subject:

From 20 April to 21 June 2026, the Commission ran the campaign ‘Protect what matters: our democracy’ (with the involvement of the agencies Havas Paris, Havas Play, Havas Media, Prose on Pixels), securing over 75 440 outdoor advertising spaces in 3 650 cities across all 27 Member States. In statements to the media, the European Commission representation in Estonia quoted figures of approximately EUR 3 million for content creation and production and EUR 30 million for media placement, adding that a breakdown by Member State would not provide a complete picture. 1.
Can the Commission confirm or correct the sums quoted and can it indicate the budget line used, with a breakdown by type of expenditure and by Member State?
If the Commission deems it impossible to provide a country-by-country breakdown, can it say why a campaign of this magnitude can dispense with country-by-country cost transparency?

Can the Commission specify when, and pursuant to which legal instrument, the decision was taken to undertake the campaign, and under which contractual framework (framework agreement, dynamic purchasing system, specific contract) the agencies involved were engaged?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.10.2026) The campaign ‘Protect what matters: our democracy’ is funded by the budget for corporate communication actions, set out in the 2023 Communication to the Commission on ‘Corporate communication action in 2024-2027 under the Multiannual Financial Framework 20212027’1. The net media buying budget across Member States ranges between EUR 78 000 and EUR 3.5 million. Variations between countries mainly depend on population size and average media costs. The Commission has a responsibility to inform EU citizens and communicate about its activities. Protecting democracy is at the core of the Commission’s political priorities for 2024-20292. It is therefore also a communication priority for the Commission services, as outlined in the 2023 Communication. The creative strategy and asset development, and media planning and buying services were provided and purchased, respectively, under the framework contracts COMM-B1-DPS-2022-002-003 with Havas Paris and COMM-DGFWC-2023-30 with Havas Media France concluded further to call for tenders in line with the provisions of the Financial Regulation3. For detailed budget breakdowns, both parties are bound by terms of confidentiality under the terms of our framework contract. Publishing such information may reveal the contractor’s pricing model, margins, discounts, or commercial strategy, thereby prejudicing its legitimate commercial interests. This may distort fair competition between economic operators.
